chunks: What the Sheikh—may Allah the Exalted support him—transmitted to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim:
He said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about a dog that contacts something of a man's body. He said: "He should wash the place it contacted."

key_terms.اَلْكَلْبِ: the dog (classified as an 'ayn najis — an intrinsically impure substance — in Shia fiqh)
key_terms.اَلْمَكَانَ: the place/area (the specific body site that was contacted, not the whole body)
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he should wash (obligatory single washing to restore ritual purity)
key_terms.يُصِيبُ: contacts/touches (any physical contact sufficient to transfer najasah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia Islam when a dog touches part of a person's body, according to Imam al-Sadiq in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Abu Abd Allah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the case in which a dog makes contact with part of a man's body. The Imam issued a concise legal ruling: the person must wash the specific area touched, affirming the najasah (ritual impurity) of dogs as a foundational principle of Shia jurisprudence on taharah.
